intro: Serbia is a landlocked country where the Danube meets the Sava, with flat farmland in the north and mountains in the south.

chapters.title: Plains and mountains
text: Belgrade stands where the Sava flows into the Danube. North of the capital, the province of Vojvodina is part of the flat, fertile Pannonian Plain; the south is hilly and mountainous. On the border with Romania, the Danube cuts through the dramatic Iron Gates gorge.
Serbia borders Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Croatia, as well as Kosovo, whose independence it disputes.

chapters.title: Climate
text: Serbia has hot summers and cold winters, with snow in the mountains, where ski resorts such as Kopaonik are popular.
